questions.prompt: A technician enters the following commands on a Cisco switch. What is the technician configuring?

structuredBlocks.content:
SwitchA(config)# interface vlan 1
SwitchA(config-if)# ip address 192.168.1.1 255.255.255.0
SwitchA(config-if)# no shutdown

explanation.conceptRefresher: A Layer 2 switch does not route packets between physical ports by default, but requires an SVI (commonly VLAN 1) to be reachable via SSH, Telnet, or web management.

questions.prompt: Refer to the exhibit. An administrator is trying to configure the switch but receives the error message that is displayed in the exhibit. What is the problem?

options.text: The entire command, configure terminal, must be used.
The administrator is already in global configuration mode.
The administrator must first enter privileged EXEC mode before issuing the command.
The administrator must connect via the console port to access global configuration mode.

explanation.answerReasoning: The prompt "Switch1>" indicates the switch is in user EXEC mode. The command "configure terminal" (or shorthand "config t") is only available in privileged EXEC mode ("Switch1#").
explanation.conceptRefresher: To enter privileged EXEC mode, the administrator must enter the "enable" command at the user EXEC prompt ("Switch1>").

questions.prompt: [DEV FIXTURE] Which two protocols operate at the transport layer of the TCP/IP model? (Choose two.)

explanation.answerReasoning: TCP and UDP are the primary transport layer protocols in the TCP/IP suite. IP and ARP operate at the Internet/network layer.
explanation.conceptRefresher: TCP provides connection-oriented reliable delivery; UDP provides lightweight, connectionless datagram delivery.
